photosynthetic capacity increased with leaf expansion in both species, but the rate of increase was greater in olive than in the deciduous peach, and that photosynthetic rates were higher in olive than in deciduous peach.

the photosynthetic capacity in the leaves of a deciduous mesophile fruit tree (Pr. persica) and in the leaves of an evergreen sclero-phyllous Mediterranean shrub tree (Oe. europaea) increases as leaves approach full expansion, and that the internal CO2 transfer conductances correlate with photosynthetic capacities, although differences between species are only partially explained by structural and anatomical leaf traits.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the relative importance of internal architecture, biochemical leaf traits, and stomatal control on photosynthetic efficiency of two contrasting woody species.
how the photosynthetic capacity and mesophyll structure of the two woody species are affected by their different developmental strategies.
the relationship between leaf structure and function, and how this is modified during leaf development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photosynthetic capacity is a complex trait, which is not simply a function of leaf anatomy or leaf mass per unit area.
the photosynthetic capacity is a function of leaf expansion and that it is determined by a complex combination of leaf anatomical and physiological properties.
photosynthetic capacity was more dependent on mesophyll traits than on leaf structural traits during the development of peach and olive foliage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photosynthetic apparatus in the two species was optimized to the same extent, although, with different strategies for resource partitioning.
photosynthetic efficiency in these woody species is not only determined by the leaf mass per area (LMA) ratio and N content but also by the internal leaf structure and its development.

the mesophyll anatomy, and not the LMA, is the most important determinant of photosynthetic capacity and that the mesophyllic structure of leaves is a key element of the functional adaptation of plants to the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the case of woody plants, the relative contribution of the different components of the photosynthetic apparatus to the overall photosynthetic performance of the leaf depends on the species-specific developmental pattern of leaves.
the photosynthetic capacity is a function of the leaf anatomy and physiology, and the relative importance of these traits would depend on a plant’s adaptation to its environment.
, the photosynthetic capacity in the course of leaf ontogeny in the two woody species studied is mainly determined by mesophyll properties and not by LMA.
